overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving insufficiently detailed minutes for four executive sessions and by failing to periodically review executive session minutes, but found no violation for six other sets and declined to find an intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to periodically review ten sets of executive session minutes (2010-2018) for release to the public.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals to determine if continued non-disclosure was warranted.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that executive session minutes for June 8, 2010, March 11, 2014, June 13, 2017, and November 9, 2018 were insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving insufficiently detailed minutes of its June 8, 2010, March 11, 2014, June 13, 2017, and November 9, 2018, executive sessions.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged insufficiently detailed executive session minutes for August and September 2012 and June, July 2015 sessions.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law with respect to the August 14, 2012, August 28, 2012, September 11, 2012, June 9, 2015, June 30, 2015, and July 14, 2015, executive session meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board's executive session minutes often omitted start and adjournment times.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by omitting this information from the executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged executive session minutes did not specify attendees' full names.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, we have not construed the Open Meeting Law as requiring meeting minutes to specify the first and last names of those present at executive sessions.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the insufficient minutes were an intentional violation forming a pervasive pattern to conceal police matters.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to find an intentional violation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.

Amend, to the best of its ability, the executive session minutes for June 8, 2010, March 11, 2014, June 13, 2017, and November 9, 2018, and release them to the public unless lawfully withheld under G.L. c. 30A, § 22(f).
To the extent feasible, add a list of documents used to each set of the amended minutes.
Within 90 days of receipt of the letter, certify to the AG's office that the minutes have been amended and released.
remedy_passage: we order the Board to amend, to the best of its ability, the executive session minutes as described above, and to release those minutes to the public, unless any portion thereof may lawfully be withheld in accordance with G.L. c. 30A, § 22(f).
